extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from XML sections and figure captions; claims are limited to direct membrane-disruption/localization/morphology evidence in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NCR247 and NCR335 directly increase bacterial membrane permeability in S. enterica and L. monocytogenes under the Live/Dead BacLight SYTO-9/PI assay conditions reported here.
direct_assay_types: Live/Dead BacLight SYTO-9/PI confocal membrane permeability assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Qualitative microscopy evidence; no numeric permeability percentage is extracted from local material.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: FITC-labeled NCR247 and NCR335 in S. enterica and L. monocytogenes
mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC localization shows peptide accumulation in S. enterica cytoplasm and membrane-overlap localization in L. monocytogenes, supporting species-dependent membrane interaction/localization behavior.
direct_assay_types: FITC-labeled peptide confocal localization with FM4-64 membrane staining
mechanism_claims.limitations: Localization is qualitative; it does not by itself prove a specific intracellular molecular target.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: NCR247 and NCR335 effects on S. enterica and L. monocytogenes cell morphology
mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM evidence supports membrane-surface damage, blebbing/roughening, and lysis outcomes after NCR247/NCR335 exposure, consistent with membrane disruption leading to cell death.
direct_assay_types: scanning electron microscopy of peptide-treated bacteria
mechanism_claims.limitations: Does not promote the introduction/discussion references to DNA/RNA/protein synthesis or prior NCR247 intracellular targets as direct mechanisms in this paper.
